doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Giving up film backgrounds
summary: Mandel explains he stopped wanting to write film backgrounds through the 1970s and 80s, preferring records, and may do pops concerts.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So, you told me recently that you basically weren’t interested in writing, quote “backgrounds for films anymore.”
I am not, at all, I’ve done it.
When did you make that decision?

I’ve been working towards that decision all through the 80s, even – I started getting very disenchanted with it in the 70s, I keep thinking of movies I did during that, as I talk about it, that I remember around the time I was doing, Freaky Friday, and, Escape to Witch Mountain out at Disney I was staring to really want to do records more and films, I’d have loved to have gotten rid of films. I don’t like writing background, that much and developing – I’ve never wanted to personally write large works, symphonies, concert pieces or I’d have done it. ‘Cause developing material is, I can do it, I’ve certainly had to do it enough for movies, but it’s not really what I get the most satisfaction out of.
Because it struck me that you’d be a natural to do say what Mancini did and go out and do orchestra pops concerts and do your medley of hits.
Because I mean, you’ve probably got as many great tunes that people are aware of as Hank did, if you were to go down the list of them.
